decision: keep both anchors (no actions): the ORCID most likely belongs to Robert Hogg, a University of Queensland historian of gender and sexuality, and the JMIR papers carry it in error
evidence: The public ORCID record 0000-0002-7481-4010 gives the name 'Robert Hogg' and shows no works, employment or biography. It was created 2018-01-23 by member referral, and the owner has claimed it. In Crossref the only item that also gives an affiliation is the Journal of Religious History review (online 2018-03-12) of de Groot and Morgan, Sex, Gender and the Sacred, by 'Robert Hogg, University of Queensland'. That fits Robert Hogg, UQ lecturer in Australian Studies and historian of masculinity and sexuality (Men and Manliness on the Frontier: Queensland and British Columbia, Palgrave 2012, from his 2007 UQ thesis). The JMIR papers (2018-2021, Vancouver gay and bisexual men's health studies) name 'Robert S Hogg', the BC Centre for Excellence in HIV/AIDS epidemiologist, who already has his own ORCID 0000-0003-3463-5488. None of the JMIR ORCID assertions is authenticated, so they are publisher-entered errors. So the key's person is a historian, but the six JMIR works (w-1483711 to w-1483716) should be withdrawn from p-19156. Wikidata Q88294536 is a bot item built from this ORCID: it carries only the ORCID, and its label 'Robert S Hogg' copies the mis-tagged papers. It names the same ORCID holder, so it is not detached, but its label is unreliable. Not certain enough to detach anything. p-47762 (AHA PhD 'Hogg, Robert') was not examined.
